q: For Group A dwellings, what is the minimum depth of a footing as required by the Building Code?
n: Footings of Group A dwellings must be at least 600 mm below the ground surface. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VII, Sec. 708.

q: What is the minimum bar size for column longitudinal reinforcement?
n: Column longitudinal bars are commonly at least 16 mm, the usual practical minimum in Philippine practice. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 410; Philippine design practice.

q: What is the minimum bar size for column ties (main bars 32 mm or smaller)?
n: Column ties must be at least 10 mm bars for longitudinal bars up to 32 mm (12 mm for larger bars). Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 425.7.2.2.

q: Asatule of thumb, the beam width should be__ the column width.
n: Beams are usually no wider than the columns they frame into, so their bars pass inside the column cage. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 418.6.2 (beam width limits); detailing practice.

q: Based on standard structural design guidelines, what is the minimum recommended size for a reinforced concrete column to ensure stability and adequate load-bearing capacity?
n: A common minimum size for RC columns in Philippine practice is 200 × 300 mm, enough for bars, cover and stability. Source: NSCP 2015 Chapter 4; Philippine design practice.

q: What is a column that doesn't line up with the column below it?
n: A planted column does not line up with the column below. It sits on a transfer beam or girder. Source: Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture.

q: What is the largest axial load a column can carry, in theory, before it buckles?
n: The critical buckling load (Euler load, Pcr = π²EI/(KL)²) is the theoretical maximum axial load before a column buckles. Source: Gere & Goodno, Mechanics of Materials.

q: What does a column's slenderness ratio mainly determine?
n: The slenderness ratio (kL/r) mainly determines a column's tendency to buckle. A high ratio means buckling governs over crushing. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 406.2.5; Gere & Goodno, Mechanics of Materials.

q: What is a steel pipe column filled with concrete commonly called?
n: A steel pipe column filled with concrete is commonly called a Lally column. Source: Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture.

q: What do you call a column that raises or supports a structure above ground level?
n: A pier is a column-like support that raises a structure above ground level. Source: Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture.

q: What wood column is a single piece of square or rectangular section?
n: A solid (solid-sawn) wood column is a single piece of square or rectangular section. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated; NSCP 2015 Chapter 6.

q: What thick column tends to fail by crushing rather than buckling?
n: Short, stocky columns fail by crushing of the material, not by buckling. Source: Gere & Goodno, Mechanics of Materials.

q: What is it called when a straight column under compression suddenly deflects sideways?
n: Buckling is the sudden sideways deflection of a straight column under compression. Source: Gere & Goodno, Mechanics of Materials.

q: Ties are used mainly in:
n: Ties are used mainly in columns, to hold the longitudinal bars and confine the concrete. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 425.7.2.

q: Which force tends to shorten a member?
n: Compression shortens a member. Tension lengthens it. Compression pushes the particles of a member together, as in columns and the top fibres of a sagging beam. Source: Gere & Goodno, Mechanics of Materials.

q: What typically happens to a short column under load?
n: A short column deforms by crushing under load rather than buckling. Source: Gere & Goodno, Mechanics of Materials.

q: Which column is most likely to fail by buckling?
n: Long (slender) columns are most likely to fail by buckling. Source: Gere & Goodno, Mechanics of Materials.

q: Which column commonly fails by crushing?
n: Short columns commonly fail by crushing. A short column is stocky enough that its material crushes before it can buckle sideways. Source: Gere & Goodno, Mechanics of Materials.

q: A long column is designed mainly against:
n: Long columns are designed mainly against buckling, because stability governs. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 406.6 (slenderness effects).

q: Which column shape is considered the most efficient for structural performance?
n: A circular section has equal stiffness in every direction and resists buckling equally about any axis, so it is the most efficient column shape. Source: Gere & Goodno, Mechanics of Materials; Schodek, Structures.

q: What is the main purpose of a post base in column construction?
o: To prevent corrosion of the steel
To anchor the column to a slab-on-grade
To transmit the load from the column to the footing
n: A post base transmits the column load to the footing and anchors the post, keeping wood clear of moisture. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: Which reinforcement in an RC column resists lateral forces and confines the core?
n: Lateral ties (or spirals) confine the column core, restrain bar buckling and resist lateral (shear) forces. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 425.7.2 and 418.7.5.

q: What is the typical job of a column?
o: Carrying axial loads from beams and slabs to the foundation
n: A column carries axial loads from beams and slabs down to the foundation. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: Why is concrete cover provided over column bars?
n: Concrete cover protects reinforcing bars from corrosion and fire, and provides bond. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 420.6.1.

q: What is the maximum usable strain at the extreme concrete compression fiber?
n: NSCP and ACI take the maximum usable strain at the extreme concrete compression fibre as 0.003. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 422.2.2.1.

q: What is the required maximum finished dimension of wooden supports for a one-storey house having a total maximum height of 5.50 m and spacing of post at 3.60 m as per national building code?
n: Table VII.5 gives 125 × 125 mm (0.125 × 0.125 m) wooden posts for a 1-storey house of 5.50 m total height with posts spaced 3.60 m. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VII, Table VII.5.

q: Under NSCP 2015, what is the strength reduction factor for bearing on concrete?
n: NSCP 2015, following ACI 318-14, uses a strength reduction factor φ = 0.65 for bearing on concrete. The older code used 0.70. Source: NSCP 2015, Table 421.2.1.

q: What is the minimum number of longitudinal bars in a spiral column?
n: Spiral columns need at least 6 longitudinal bars. Rectangular or circular tied columns need 4. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 410.7.3.1.

q: What is the minimum clear spacing between parallel bars in a beam layer?
n: Clear spacing between parallel bars in a layer must be at least 25 mm, one bar diameter, or 4/3 of the maximum aggregate size. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 425.2.1.

q: What is a beam fixed at one end and free at the other?
n: A cantilever beam is fixed at one end and free at the other. Its fixed end resists both moment and shear, as in balconies and canopies. Source: Hibbeler, Structural Analysis.

q: Why are inverted beams used?
o: To minimize surface cracking in the beam
To provide added strength in cantilevered roofs
n: Inverted (upstand) beams sit above the slab, leaving a clear soffit below for headroom. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: What beam, below or above grade, ties two members together to keep them from spreading?
n: A tie beam, below or above grade, ties two members (such as footings) together to keep them from spreading. Source: Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture.

q: What beam spans over a door or window opening?
n: A lintel beam spans over a door or window opening, carrying the wall above. Source: Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture.

q: Which column has a continuous helical bar around its longitudinal bars?
n: A spiral column has a continuous helical bar wrapped around its longitudinal bars. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 425.7.3.
